title: Anchor-based staged exposure controller and failback safety layer
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: Current staged rollouts rely on fixed step schedules and simple traffic splits. We see noisy telemetry when KV cache warm-up, heterogeneous user sessions, and transient infra degradation interact with staged exposures. Goals: 1) Introduce an 'anchor' concept — a pinned stable cohort (~1-3% of requests) always served by the incumbent to preserve baseline user experience and provide a ground-truth signal. 2) Implement an exposure controller that drives incremental traffic to candidates using multiplicative steps (exponential exposure curve) with built-in cooling windows, and that factors in warm-up signals (KV hit rate, cache latency) before progressing. 3) Add a layered failback/safety system: automatic rollback triggers based on immediate metric breaches, and a graceful failback path that can partially retreat exposure rather than a full rollback when degradation is small but non-zero. 4) Support combined modes: A/B splits, shadow warming, and anchor-aware traffic routing. Deliverable: policy engine + DSL and runtime glue, plus observability dashboards and test harness for offline simulation.
acceptance_criteria: DSL defined for anchor ratio, initial step, multiplier, max exposure, cooldown window and rollback hysteresis
Controller implementation routes traffic per policy and respects anchor cohort (anchor traffic always to baseline model)
Shadow warming integration: candidate receives identical requests in shadow; KV cache warm-up metrics available and factored into progression decisions
Automated rollback triggers: p95 latency increase > 20% OR absolute error rate > 0.5% OR eval-quality drop > 3% compared to anchor baseline
Partial retreat path: when degradation is between warning and rollback thresholds, controller halves exposure and waits cooldown instead of immediate rollback
End-to-end tests and sim harness validate exposure curves across synthetic user mixes and cache cold-start scenarios
Dashboard panels for anchor vs candidate baselines, exposure curve, rollback events and shadow warm-up metrics
design_notes: Anchor cohort is a small persistent routing group (configurable); it must be excluded from statistical significance calculations for the candidate exposure but used as a baseline comparator
We prefer multiplicative step progression (x2) with a max of 25% exposure by default; additive steps yield slower warm-up for models with long KV warm-up times

Shadow traffic warm-up window: candidate receives shadow traffic at full rate but does not respond to users. We track KV cache hit-rate and median cache latency; only advance exposure after warm-up threshold met
Rollback hysteresis: require metric stabilization for a min_hold (e.g., 10 minutes) before rollback; support immediate rollback for critical breaches (SLA loss)
Costs: shadow warming increases cost ~1.8x during warm window; policy must respect tenant cost ceilings if provided
rollout_policy_dsl_example:
# Example DSL (YAML-like)
exposure_policy: 
  anchor_ratio: 0.02
  initial_exposure: 0.005
  step_multiplier: 2.0
  max_exposure: 0.25
  cooldown_minutes: 30
  min_hold_minutes: 10
guards:
  p95_latency_pct_increase: 20
  error_rate_absolute: 0.005
  eval_score_drop_pct: 3
actions:
  on_warning: "halve_exposure_and_cooldown"
  on_critical: "immediate_full_rollback"
shadow_warmup:
  enabled: true
  warmup_traffic_fraction: 1.0
  required_kv_hit_rate: 0.6
  required_kv_median_latency_ms: 25
monitoring_triggers: p95 latency increase relative to anchor > 20% triggers critical rollback
absolute error rate increase > 0.5% triggers critical rollback
eval set score drop > 3% triggers critical rollback
KV cache hit-rate below configured threshold prevents progression
consecutive cold-starts > 3 within 30m should pause progression and mark for manual review
test_plan: Unit tests for DSL parser and policy evaluator
Integration test: simulate user mixes (short/long sessions) with KV warm-up behavior and verify exposure progression matches expected curve
Chaos test: inject transient infra latency and ensure hysteresis prevents oscillation between progress and rollback
Cost-limited test: tenant cost cap prevents shadow warming above configured threshold
Dry-run mode in staging: exercise full policy with real telemetry and record decisions for audit
